item.title: Git Refs and Refspecs: Grammar Reference
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: Git’s ref system is a tiny language for naming objects and mapping them across repositories. This post is a grammar reference first, and examples second. Grammar reference Ref and refname ref := 'refs/' refpath refpath := name ('/' name)* name := 1+ valid-char valid-char := printable ASCII EXCEPT {space, control, '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\'} constraints := not (leading '/', trailing '/', '//', '..', '.lock', '@{') Common namespaces (grammar applies equally):

item.title: Git Bash and WSL on Windows Terminal Preview vs IntelliJ
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: For some reason IntelliJ and Windows terminal discover available shells in different ways, but either way is not ideal. (In-fact IntelliJ uses two different means of discovery.) The terminal popup in Intellj seems to be unaware of Gitbash.. Which is in complete contrast to the terminal settings (same plugin) which is unaware of my WSL deployments. (Possibly because it’s using a file path based system) Which means I can’t set Debian WSL as my default terminal in IntelliJ.
